APPLICATION OF Sayres McAlpin FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF himself IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. POST OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: Kasaan, Alaska Date of enrollment, September 30, 1918 Term of enrollment, three (3) years. NAME OF COLLECTING AGENT: Position, APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wn., of Sayres McAlpin, male, I, Sayres McAlpin, of Kasan, P.O., State of Alaska, do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to his enrollment in said school for a period of three years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Butler, Pa., on Dec. 25, 1901; that the father, Kenneth McAlpin, was a White, Tribe located at XXXXXXXXX Agency; that he left the tribe about XXXXXXXXX; that the mother, Agnes McAlpin Thompson was a Black Indian of the Hyda Tribe located at Kasan, Alaska, Agency, and left the tribe about XXXXXXXXX; that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:

I hereby certify that on May 21st, 1919, I made a careful examination of the physical condition of Joyce McAlpin, the child named in the foregoing application, and found him to be in poor physical condition to attend school. I therefore recommend that the said child be enrolled in this school. This 21st day of May 21st, 1919 Cleard P. Kincaid, M.D. School Physician INDORSEMENT. A child showing one-sixteenth or less Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, Indian fashion, who, if debarred from the Government schools, could not obtain an education, may be permitted in the reservation day and boarding schools, but it is preferable that it be not transferred to a nonreservation school, without special permission from the Office. Children showing one-eighth or less Indian blood, whose parents do not live on an Indian reservation, whose home is among white people where there are churches and schools, who are presumed to have adopted the white man's manners and customs, and are to all intents and purposes white people, are debarred from enrollment in the Government nonreservation and reservation schools. Superintendents, in all cases where doubt exists as to the degree of Indian blood of a child proposed for transfer, should fully satisfy themselves of the facts by affidavits from reliable persons, which affidavits must be kept on file at the school. A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both Superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and Superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. A pupil dismissed from school for cause must not be enrolled in any other school without the permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Full facts must be submitted with each request. Itasaan, Alaska Oct. 22, 1919 Mr. Superintendent, Please give bearer (my son Walter Young) $45.00 sent you, for transportation for my grandsons Paul and Jayros McAlpine. Walter will need the money for the Tombstone I am sending him to get. Very Respectfully, Mrs. Paul Young. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Nov. 3, 1919 Mrs. Paul Young Kasaan, Alaska Dear Madam: I am enclosing herewith checks No. 900 and No. 901 in the sum of $22.50 each. This is in accordance with your letter of October 22, 1919, requesting $45.00, the transportation for Paul and Sayres McAlpin. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. Reproduced at the National Archives at Seattle 329 Sayres McAlpin Cushman School Tacoma Wash. Mrs. Paul Young Havana Ala. Reproduced at the National Archives at Seattle Kasaan Alaska July 1, 1918 My dear Grandsons: We are just about ready to go to Hitekikan for the Fourth of July. And I'm sorry that you boys are not here. Yankee has been buying fish all spring but hasn't much money. I'm sending $1 & $5.00 for both of you to come up on, as I know you will earn money to buy you some clothes next fall and go back to school. I'm not feeling well since the death of your Grandpa, and I want you boys once to be with me this summer. I hope the aupt. would not hold you. Have the aupt. buy your tickets. Take good care of yourselves with love your Grandma Mrs. Paul Young P.S. When you boys start from school come right home do not stay around Seattle have the Supst of the school buy you tickets so your boys won't have hard time the canner just start to from till the supst that I want your boys home this summer and go back in fall when the school start Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., July 21, 1919 Mrs. Paul Young Kasaan, Alaska Dear Madam: Enclosed herewith find Official Receipt No. 176048 for deposit of $22.50 for Sayres McAlpin, and $22.50 for Paul McAlpin. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG MG. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Nov. 8, 1918. Mr. Edward Young, Kasnan, Alaska. Dear Sir: In reply to your inquiry of October 25th regarding your grandson Bayres McAlpin, would advise that he has fully recovered from influenza and is now well. He received careful attention and excellent care while he was ill to get him well as soon as possible and to prevent him from getting pneumonia. Tell his grandmother that the boy is now all right, and she should not worry about him. Yours very sincerely, Superintendent Not sick now - Fully recovered from influenza Hassan Alaska Oct. 25, 1918. Dear Sir: We just heard that "Sayers Mc Alpin" is sick. If he is sick please let us know how he is getting along, as his grandma is worried over him. And will you please see that their boys write home every month, we haven't heard from them since they left home. It worries the old folks very much. Hoping that you will answer this letter soon. Yours truly, Edward Young. CASE RECORD. NAME: Loyal M. C. Alpian Sex: Male Tribe: [redacted] State: Wash.
